q.t: In a right triangle, the side opposite θ is 3, the side next to θ is 4 and the hypotenuse is 5. Find sin θ.
q.e: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

q.t: In the same triangle (opposite 3, adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5), find cos θ.
q.e: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 4/5.

q.t: In the same triangle (opposite 3, adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5), find tan θ.
q.e: tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent = 3/4.

q.t: If sin θ = 5/13, find cos θ (θ acute).
q.e: Opposite 5, hypotenuse 13, so adjacent = √(169 − 25) = 12; cos θ = 12/13.

q.t: sec θ is the reciprocal of…
q.e: sec θ = hypotenuse ÷ adjacent, which is cos θ turned upside down.

q.t: If tan θ = 1, find cot θ.
q.e: cot θ = 1/tan θ = 1/1.

q.t: Find sin² θ + cos² θ for any angle θ.
q.e: (opp² + adj²)/hyp² = hyp²/hyp² = 1, by Pythagoras.

q.t: If cosec θ = 2, find sin θ.
q.e: sin θ is the reciprocal of cosec θ.

q.t: tan θ equals sin θ divided by…
q.e: (opp/hyp) ÷ (adj/hyp) = opp/adj = tan θ — the hypotenuses cancel.

q.t: If cos A = 0.6, find sec A.
If tan θ = 8/15, find sin θ.
q.e: Opposite 8, adjacent 15, so hypotenuse = √(64 + 225) = 17.

q.t: If sin A = 3/5, find tan A + sec A.
q.e: Adjacent = 4: tan A = 3/4, sec A = 5/4, total 8/4.

q.t: If cot θ = 7/24, find cos θ.
q.e: Adjacent 7, opposite 24, hypotenuse 25, so cos θ = 7/25.

q.t: If sec θ = 13/12, find cosec θ.
q.e: Hypotenuse 13, adjacent 12, so opposite 5; cosec θ = 13/5.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with AB = 24 and BC = 7. Find sin A cos C + cos A sin C.
If 3 tan θ = 4, find (4 sin θ − cos θ)/(4 sin θ + cos θ).
If 4 cot θ = 3, find (sin θ + cos θ)/(sin θ − cos θ).
Can sin θ = 4/3 for some angle θ?
o: No — sin θ can never be more than 1
q.e: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, and the hypotenuse is the longest side.

q.t: If tan θ = 1 (θ acute), find sin θ × cos θ.
q.e: Opposite = adjacent = 1, hypotenuse √2: sin θ = cos θ = 1/√2, product 1/2.

q.t: ΔPQR is right-angled at Q. PR + QR = 18 cm and PQ = 6 cm. Find sin P.
q.e: PR² − QR² = 36, so (PR − QR) × 18 = 36 and PR − QR = 2. So PR = 10, QR = 8: sin P = 8/10.

q.t: If sin θ = 5/13, find (sec θ + tan θ)/(sec θ − tan θ).
If cot θ = 15/8, find ((2 + 2 sin θ)(1 − sin θ))/((1 + cos θ)(2 − 2 cos θ)).
q.e: It simplifies to 2(1 − sin² θ)/2(1 − cos² θ) = cos² θ/sin² θ = cot² θ.

q.t: If tan θ = 3/2, find (3 sin θ − 2 cos θ)/(3 sin θ + 2 cos θ).
q.e: Divide top and bottom by cos θ: (3 tan θ − 2)/(3 tan θ + 2) = (4.5 − 2)/(4.5 + 2) = 2.5/6.5.

q.t: If sin θ = a/b, then tan θ equals…
q.e: Opposite a, hypotenuse b, so adjacent √(b² − a²); tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at C and tan A = 1/√3. Find cos A cos B − sin A sin B.
If cosec A = 2, find 1/tan A + sin A/(1 + cos A).
If tan θ = 12/5, find (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ).
ΔABC is right-angled at B with AB = 12 cm and sin A = 5/13. Find its perimeter.
q.e: BC/AC = 5/13 with AB = 12 means the 5–12–13 triangle: BC = 5, AC = 13.

q.t: If 3 cot A = 4, find (1 − tan² A)/(1 + tan² A).
If x = 3 cos θ and y = 4 sin θ, find x²/9 + y²/16.
q.e: x²/9 = cos² θ and y²/16 = sin² θ, which add to 1.

q.t: If tan θ = 8/15, find (1 − sin θ + cos θ)/(1 + sin θ + cos θ).
If sin θ = (m² − n²)/(m² + n²), then tan θ equals…
q.e: Adjacent² = (m² + n²)² − (m² − n²)² = 4m²n², so adjacent = 2mn.

q.t: If 5 sin² θ + 3 cos² θ = 4 (θ acute), find tan θ.
q.e: Write 3 cos² θ = 3 − 3 sin² θ: 2 sin² θ + 3 = 4, so sin² θ = 1/2 and θ = 45°.

q.t: If sec θ = x + 1/(4x), then sec θ + tan θ equals…
q.e: tan² θ = sec² θ − 1 = (x − 1/(4x))², so tan θ = ±(x − 1/(4x)). Adding to sec θ gives 2x or 1/(2x).

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with AC + AB = 9 cm and BC = 3 cm. Find sec A + tan A.
q.e: AC² − AB² = 9, so (AC − AB) × 9 = 9 and AC − AB = 1: AC = 5, AB = 4. sec A = 5/4, tan A = 3/4.

q.t: If cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ, then cos θ − sin θ equals…
q.e: sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ, so cos θ = sin θ/(√2 − 1) = (√2 + 1) sin θ. Then cos θ − sin θ = √2 sin θ.

q.t: If tan A = n tan B and sin A = m sin B, then cos² A equals…
q.e: From the two facts, cos B = n cos A/m and sin B = sin A/m. Put both into sin² B + cos² B = 1 and solve for cos² A.

q.t: If sin θ = 1/3, find 2 cot² θ + 2.
q.e: 2 cot² θ + 2 = 2(1 + cot² θ) = 2 cosec² θ = 2 × 9.

q.t: If tan θ = 1/√5, find (cosec² θ − sec² θ)/(cosec² θ + sec² θ).
q.e: cosec² θ = 1 + cot² θ = 6, sec² θ = 1 + tan² θ = 6/5: (24/5)/(36/5).

q.t: If cos θ = 0.6, find 5 sin θ − 3 tan θ.
q.e: sin θ = 0.8 and tan θ = 4/3: 4 − 4 = 0.
